import BanditRLProof.OnlineStrongConvexSupport
import BanditRLProof.OnlinePrescientBregmanSource
import Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Group.Finset.Basic

noncomputable section
open Set Finset
namespace BanditRL.OnlineConvex

theorem cumulative_optimistic_stability {E : Type*}
    [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    (V : Set E) (hV : Convex ℝ V)
    (psi hint : E → ℝ) (loss : ℕ → E → EReal) (n : ℕ) (lam : ℝ)
    (hbot : ∀ i < n + 1, ∀ x, loss i x ≠ ⊥)
    (hdom : ∀ i < n + 1, V ⊆ effectiveDomain (loss i))
    (hlam : 0 ≤ lam)
    (hstrong : let G : E → EReal := fun x =>
        (psi x : EReal) + ∑ i ∈ range (n + 1), loss i x + extendedIndicator V x
      ∀ x ∈ V, ∀ y ∈ V, ∀ a : ℝ, 0 < a → a < 1 →
        G (a • x + (1 - a) • y) ≤
          (a : EReal) * G x + ((1 - a : ℝ) : EReal) * G y -
            (((lam / 2) * a * (1 - a) * ‖x - y‖ ^ 2 : ℝ) : EReal))
    (p : E) (hp : p ∈ V)
    (hprediction : IsMinOn (fun x =>
      (psi x : EReal) + ∑ i ∈ range n, loss i x + (hint x : EReal)) V p)
    (g : E →L[ℝ] ℝ)
    (hdifference : ∀ z ∈ V,
      (loss n p).toReal - hint p + g (z - p) ≤ (loss n z).toReal - hint z)
    (q : E) (hq : q ∈ V) :
    let G : E → EReal := fun x =>
      (psi x : EReal) + ∑ i ∈ range (n + 1), loss i x + extendedIndicator V x
    (G p).toReal - (G q).toReal ≤
      g (p - q) - (lam / 2) * ‖p - q‖ ^ 2

end BanditRL.OnlineConvex

source_delta: This is the sharp local stability implication in the finite common-domain branch of Lemma7.5 and Theorem7.47, not either complete numbered result. Source Algorithm7.8 only requires the played point to lie in the current loss domain; common finiteness on V is an explicit branch qualification. Algorithm15.9 already prints the common-domain condition. Local continuous-dual support is weaker than source global coordinate subgradient membership; only the global-to-local implication is intended. The ambient arbitrary real normed space generalizes the source finite-dimensional conditional inequality; no finite-dimensional attainment claim follows. The header assumes total-objective curvature, not regularizer-only curvature. n=0, lambda=0 and nonzero g are allowed. The actual prediction minimum supplies p, not a hidden minimum of G. No closedness, support-existence or attainment conclusion is supplied.
implementation_spine: First use no-bottom and below-top together to obtain finite real values of every included loss on V. Induct over the prefix to establish no-bottom globally and exact real finite-sum identities on V. The indicator makes G top outside V; p in V provides the witness for sourceProper_of_domain on this actual G. For z in V, add A(p)+hint(p)<=A(z)+hint(z) from the prediction minimum to loss_n(p)-hint(p)+g(z-p)<=loss_n(z)-hint(z). Hints cancel and the finite-prefix decomposition yields G(p)+g(z-p)<=G(z). This newly produced support is passed to stronglyConvex_support_growth on the same G,V,lambda,p,g,q. Finally use linearity g(q-p)=-g(p-q) and norm symmetry to rearrange the bound. The source describes the support construction using zero support at the predicted minimum and subgradient sum inclusion; the implementation proves the same local inequality directly rather than adding public zero-support wrappers.
consumers: The closed 13-conjunct consumer uses E=R, V=[-1,1], n=0, psi(x)=x^2/2, hint=0, loss_i(x)=x, p=0, q=-1, lambda=1 and g(x)=x. It proves all component premises internally and its first conjunction genuinely applies cumulative_optimistic_stability to those exact operands. The current objective is G(x)=x^2/2+x on V and top outside. p minimizes the prediction objective but does NOT minimize G. Both sides of the sharp bound equal1/2, support is nonzero, G(0)=0, G(-1)=-1/2 and G(2)=top. It also proves the local difference-support premise and feasible/outside points. This demonstrates the missing support producer at a genuine nonminimum of G; numerical arithmetic does not replace the actual theorem call. This consumer exercises n0 and positive lambda, not all possible lambda0 or bottom-loss edge cases.
